name: NVIDIA H100 SXM
memory_bandwidth_basis: HBM3 5.2Gbps x 5120-bit = 3350 GB/s (the datasheet prints 3.35 TB/s; the HBM2e 80GB SXM2 module is 5 stacks x 1024-bit = 5120-bit at 5.2Gbps).
notes: CORRECTED 2026-10-03: no value changed; dense flags re-verified against the H100 datasheet PDF itself (source acc2-nv-h100-datasheet-2023, page-2 table footnote 2 'With sparsity'). The H100 SXM column prints TF32 989 / BFLOAT16 1,979 / FP16 1,979 / FP8 3,958 / INT8 3,958 TOPS, all SPARSE; dense is exactly half, matching the 494.5 / 989.5 / 989.5 / 1,979 / 1,979 stored here. FP64 34, FP64 Tensor 67 and FP32 67 carry no sparsity footnote and are recorded as printed. AUDIT CORRECTION: the dense/sparse flag on the tensor rows was inverted. FP16 989.5 / FP8 1979 TFLOPS are DENSE. NVIDIA prints 989 TF32 / 1,979 FP16 / 3,958 FP8 'WITH SPARITY' (sparse = 2x). These rows were previously flagged dense:false, which wrongly told a reader they were sparse.  The stored numbers are correct dense values. CRITICAL: the datasheet prints 989 TFLOPS TF32 / 1,979 BFLOAT16+FP16 / 3,958 FP8+INT8, ALL MARKED 'WITH SPARITY'. The DENSE numbers recorded here are exactly half of NVIDIA's printed sparse figures (494.5 TF32 / 989.5 BF16+FP16 / 1,979 FP8+INT8). Quoting NVIDIA's printed 1,979 'FP16 TFLOPS' as a dense figure overstates real dense throughput by 2x - and note NVIDIA's own marketing copy, the AMD MI300X page footnote and the H200 spec table all label 1,979 as the WITH-SPARITY figure, so anyone reading the sheet without the footnote halves it twice. FP64 34 and FP32 67 are dense and sparsity-independent. TDP is configurable up to 700W. NVLink 900 GB/s bidirectional per GPU. The 'other' row is FP64 34 TFLOPS (dense) - this schema's precision enum has no fp64 member.
